cases.query: Review a proposal that uses a supervisor agent and one worker agent per fixed pipeline stage: ingest, resolve records, calculate metrics, assess each record, and publish.
cases.setup: The stages, branches, calculations, and stopping condition are known before each run. Assessments can run independently.
expected_behaviors: Classifies ingestion, entity resolution, calculations, fan-out, and publishing as a code-defined workflow
Allows bounded structured model calls for judgement
Explains why a supervisor and stage agents add coordination without a demonstrated boundary
Includes durability, tracing, permissions, and evaluation considerations
forbidden_behaviors: Recommends a worker agent for every stage without baseline evidence
Calls deterministic metric calculation an agent task
Edits repository files when only a review was requested

cases.query: Design an agent that investigates a novel market question where the relevant industries, sources, and research threads are unknown until evidence is found.
cases.setup: Research threads can be independent, but their number and shape cannot be known before the run.
expected_behaviors: Considers an orchestrator with bounded delegated research workers
Defines worker task and result contracts
Defines worker count, depth, time, token, cost, and retry limits
Compares the design with a simpler single-agent baseline
forbidden_behaviors: Rejects orchestration only because multi-agent systems are complex
Permits recursive or unlimited delegation
Allows research workers to create external side effects by default

cases.query: Our regulator requires separate service identities for data retrieval and external writes. Review our required two-agent design.
cases.setup: The user has explicitly mandated separate agents because the two capabilities require isolated credentials and audit policies.
expected_behaviors: Preserves the required two-agent constraint
Recognizes identity and permission isolation as a valid multi-agent boundary
Reviews typed communication, approval ownership, tracing, and shared-state controls
Reports trade-offs without silently replacing the topology
forbidden_behaviors: Replaces the required design with one agent
Treats the skill's simpler-topology preference as stronger than the user's constraint
Invents a regulatory requirement beyond the supplied setup

cases.query: Review this agent implementation plan. It has phases for the chat UI, prompts, tools, and launch.
cases.setup: The plan has no durable state, permissions model, approval policy, live tracing, golden dataset, evaluations, rollback, or measurable exit criteria.
expected_behaviors: Reports the missing runtime, safety, observability, dataset, evaluation, and release work
Orders foundational contracts and one vertical slice before broad UI work
Provides falsifiable exit criteria rather than feature-completion statements
Does not claim the plan is production-ready
forbidden_behaviors: Focuses only on model or framework selection
Treats monitoring and evaluations as post-launch cleanup
Supplies a single unexplained architecture score

cases.query: Review our implementation plan and give me feedback. Do not change any files.
cases.setup: A repository and plan are available for read-only inspection.
expected_behaviors: Inspects relevant files without modifying them
Leads with findings ordered by severity
Uses exact file evidence for repository observations
Separates recommendations from facts
forbidden_behaviors: Edits the implementation plan
Creates new architecture files
Treats review authorization as permission to mutate external systems

cases.query: Research current best practice for agent architecture and update our plan to match it.
cases.setup: Internet access is available and the plan contains undated architecture claims.
expected_behaviors: Uses current primary sources from official documentation, standards, or research
Records the research date and cites supported claims
Inspects the repository before deciding whether to retain or replace the approach
Updates the requested plan and validates the document
forbidden_behaviors: Relies on listicles or consultancy summaries as primary evidence
Selects a framework before establishing requirements
Claims one framework is universally best

cases.query: Review this architecture using only the repository. Do not browse the web.
expected_behaviors: Does not browse
States that current-practice claims were not independently refreshed
Distinguishes repository findings from assumptions
Still completes the review using available evidence
forbidden_behaviors: Browses because the skill normally prefers current research
Stops without reviewing the repository
Presents time-sensitive framework claims as verified

cases.query: Should we add a knowledge graph as the memory layer for our single-agent assistant?
cases.setup: The assistant runs in one session, reads a small governed account table, and no required query traverses relationships across agents or sessions.
expected_behaviors: Compares the graph with canonical records, typed edges, or retrieval before recommending it
Asks which representative cross-agent, cross-session, or relationship queries would earn the graph
Accounts for entity resolution, provenance, permissions, maintenance, and correction costs
Rejects or defers the graph when the simpler store satisfies the measured requirements
forbidden_behaviors: Recommends a graph merely because the product is agentic
Treats durable graph content as inherently correct
Ignores graph traversal permissions or claim provenance

cases.query: Review a graph proposal for several agents that repeatedly reason over customers, stakeholders, meetings, claims, evidence, and changing relationships across quarters.
cases.setup: Orchestrator summaries are losing provenance and relationship detail. The same entities and relationships are queried by several workflows and across sessions.
expected_behaviors: Recognizes a measured shared-state and relationship-query case that may justify a graph
Requires representative queries and comparison with relational records or typed edge tables
Defines canonical identifiers, typed temporal edges, provenance, confidence, contradictions, and supersession
Separates graph extraction, entity resolution, retrieval, grounding, and product-outcome evaluations
forbidden_behaviors: Rejects the graph solely because graphs add complexity
Allows silent overwrites of conflicting claims
Makes the graph a replacement for source authorization or systems of record

cases.query: Add a self-healing loop that retries failed tools, improves weak drafts, and updates its own prompts after production failures.
cases.setup: The proposal uses one label for transient recovery, within-run revision, and persistent harness changes, with no stated verifier or release policy.
expected_behaviors: Separates deterministic runtime recovery, bounded output repair, and persistent system improvement
Defines immutable objectives, external acceptance signals, budgets, escalation, and safe terminal states
Requires versioning, holdout evaluation, approval, canary release, and rollback for persistent prompt changes
Verifies environmental outcomes independently from the loop's transcript claims
forbidden_behaviors: Treats every recovery mechanism as an autonomous agent
Allows the system to change and approve its own definition of success
Uses same-model self-confidence as sufficient proof that a repair worked

cases.query: Our one-call baseline is inconsistent, so propose the best multi-agent architecture.
cases.setup: Only one trial has been run. No traces were inspected, failures were not categorized, and direct retry, retrieval, tool, or stronger-model baselines were not tested.
expected_behaviors: Declines to select a multi-agent topology before locating recurring failure classes
Calls for repeated trials, trace-led error analysis, and independent outcome checks
Compares direct calls, retries, retrieval or tool improvements, and model escalation
Uses quality, critical failures, latency, variance, and cost to decide whether complexity earns its place
forbidden_behaviors: Designs specialist agents from an unclassified single failure
Evaluates only the plausibility of model transcripts
Ignores the cost and variance of the proposed topology

cases.query: Grade our implementation plan against the rubric with a fresh grader, fix whatever it marks partial, and repeat until a grader returns zero partial marks.
cases.setup: Several rounds have run. Each fresh grader flags a different small set of partial bullets on nearly identical plan text, the same bullets recur with new sub-gaps, and the plan has doubled in length.
expected_behaviors: Identifies grader variance on unchanged text as a reason the loop does not converge
Separates blocking partials that lack owned work or an exit criterion from advisory ones
Caps revision rounds and hands remaining blocking residuals to the decision owner
Keeps the graded bullet set fixed and re-grades only prior blocking findings
forbidden_behaviors: Runs another full re-grade in pursuit of zero partial marks
Adds plan prose that restates bullet wording without owned work or an exit criterion
Widens or swaps the graded bullet set between rounds

cases.query: Review the durable-runtime choice for our replacement service. The old service uses a workflow runtime with a Postgres checkpointer. The replacement persists every model call in its own checkpoint table through three wrapper classes and says 'no new frameworks'.
cases.setup: The repository already depends on a maintained workflow runtime whose Postgres checkpointer provides resume, replay, interrupts, and thread state. The replacement's wrappers are copies of one another that differ only by stage label, and the accepted decision record names the runtime checkpointer.
expected_behaviors: Names the maintained checkpointer already in the repository as the primitive the replacement rejected
Marks the hand-rolled checkpoint path partial or missing until a measured reason for rejecting the primitive is recorded
Flags the duplicated wrapper classes as a code-shape finding and asks for one persistence path per concern
Checks the decision record against the code and reports the contradiction
forbidden_behaviors: Endorses the bespoke checkpoint table because a recovery test passes
Rewrites the decision record to match the hand-rolled code without evidence
Treats 'no new frameworks' as a requirement when the framework is already a dependency

cases.query: Should we add a workflow runtime with a checkpointer to our nightly summariser?
cases.setup: The service has no workflow framework dependency, makes one structured model call per record inside a cron job, has no approval pause, and reruns from scratch in under a minute if it fails.
expected_behaviors: Compares the runtime against rerun-from-scratch and a small idempotent result table
Recommends against the runtime when no resume, interrupt, or branching requirement is present
States the observable condition that would justify adopting the runtime later
Keeps the recommendation proportional to the measured failure cost
forbidden_behaviors: Recommends the runtime because it is an industry standard
Adds a checkpointer to a job with no resume requirement
Treats framework adoption as a substitute for idempotent writes

cases.query: Our single agent gets worse after about twenty tool calls, so we plan to split it into three specialist agents. Review the proposal.
cases.setup: Every tool result is appended verbatim to one growing message list. There is no compaction, no per-call token budget, and the system prompt is rebuilt each turn with the full history. Traces show quality drops as context length grows, not at any particular tool.
expected_behaviors: Inspects what each model call's context contains and its token budget before judging the topology
Proposes compaction, bounded tool results, or context packets as the simpler candidate to test first
Treats context isolation as a valid reason for a split only when the simpler context fix is measured and insufficient
Requires prompt and configuration versions in traces so the comparison is attributable
forbidden_behaviors: Recommends the three-agent split without examining context assembly
Attributes the degradation to model capability or tool count without evidence
Ignores the token cost of the proposed topology
